title: Rabbah Zuti
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as Rav Ashi’s colleague who took a large part with him in arranging the Talmud, as in Menachot 31b, where he said to Rav Ashi: “Thus said Rabbi Yirmeyah of Difti in Rava’s name.”

There, at 52a, he said to Rav Ashi: “Come and hear.” In Beitzah 32b and Bava Batra 120a he said to Rav Ashi: “If so,” etc. In Bekhorot 36a he said to Ravina: “We teach it in the name of Rabbi Ila,” and there it reads Rava Zuti; Yuchasin’s reading is that he said it to Rav Nachman, and Hyman identifies him as the later Rav Nachman, son of Rav Huna.
He is mentioned in Bava Kamma 108b and Zevachim 24a: “Rabbah Zuti asked it thus.”
In Menachot 15b it reads Rabbi Abba Zuti, but Hyman reports that the old printings and Shitah Mekubbetzet read Rabbah Zuti; Hyman identifies Abba with Rabbah or Rava.

notes.text: The role in arranging the Talmud, later Nachman identity and Abba/Rabbah/Rava equation remain Hyman’s claims. Distinct spelling and patronymics are preserved.

The consulted Menachot 31b directly has Rabbah Zuti speaking to Rav Ashi and reporting Yirmeyah of Difti in Rava’s name. It does not itself establish a role in arranging the Talmud, the later Nachman identification or the Abba/Rabbah/Rava equation. Those claims and exact old-print/Shitah/Yuchasin variants remain Hyman’s.
